children.translated_text: Chapter on Subject Matter
Now, the absolute cessation of the threefold suffering is the supreme purpose of man. KapSs_1.1
(The nature of the supreme purpose of man)

children.text: na dṛṣṭāt tatsiddhiḥ, nivṛtte 'pyanuvṛtti darśanāt | KapSs_1.2 |
children.translated_text: That accomplishment is not from visible [means], since recurrence is observed even after cessation. KapSs_1.2
(The impossibility of cessation of suffering through worldly means)

children.text: prātyahika kṣutpratīkāravat tatpratīkāra ceṣṭanāt puruṣārthatvaṃ | KapSs_1.3 |
children.translated_text: Because the effort to counteract it is like the daily remedy for hunger, it [merely] serves a [limited] human purpose. KapSs_1.3
(The impossibility of cessation of suffering through worldly means)

children.text: sarvāsambhavāt, sambhave 'pi sattāsambhavāt heyaḥ pramāṇakuśalaiḥ | KapSs_1.4 |
children.translated_text: Because of the impossibility of [counteracting] all [suffering], and even when possible, the impossibility of permanence — it is to be rejected by those skilled in the means of valid knowledge. KapSs_1.4
(The impossibility of cessation of suffering through worldly means)
Even from excellence [of worldly means], because scripture declares the supreme excellence of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). KapSs_1.5
(The impossibility of cessation of suffering through worldly means)
And there is no distinction between the two. KapSs_1.6
(The inadequacy of Vedic means also for cessation of suffering)
For one who is bound by nature, there can be no injunction prescribing means of liberation. KapSs_1.7
(The impossibility of bondage being natural)
Because what is natural cannot be removed; the mark of invalidity is non-performance [of prescribed action]. KapSs_1.8
(The impossibility of bondage being natural)
There is no injunction for what is impossible; even when instructed, it amounts to non-instruction. KapSs_1.9
(The impossibility of bondage being natural)
Like a white cloth, or like a seed — if [you say bondage is natural but removable]. KapSs_1.10
(The impossibility of bondage being natural) — objection
Whether the power arises or does not arise, there is no instruction for what is impossible. KapSs_1.11
(The impossibility of bondage being natural) — reply

children.text: na kālayogato vyāpino nityasya sarvasambandhāt | KapSs_1.12 |
children.translated_text: Not through conjunction with time, because for an all-pervading and eternal [self], there is connection with all [times]. KapSs_1.12
Nor through conjunction with place, for the same reason. KapSs_1.13
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by time, place, or condition)
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by time, place, or condition)
Not through a particular state, because that [state] is a property of the body. KapSs_1.14
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by a particular state)
For this <s>Puruṣa</s> (self) is unattached. KapSs_1.15
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by a particular state)
Not through <s>karma</s> (action), because it is a property of something other [than the self], and because of over-extension. KapSs_1.16
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by a particular state)
The variety of experiences would be impossible if [bondage] were a property of something other [than the self]. KapSs_1.17
(The impossibility of bondage being a property of mind or body)
If [bondage is] due to the binding of <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature), then she too would be dependent. KapSs_1.18
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by Prakṛti)

children.text: na nityaśuddha buddhamukta svabhāvasya tadyogastadyogāhate | KapSs_1.19 |
children.translated_text: For one whose nature is eternally pure, awakened, and liberated, there is no conjunction with that [bondage]; such conjunction would destroy [its nature]. KapSs_1.19
(The impossibility of bondage being caused by Prakṛti)
Nor from <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), because bondage cannot result from a non-entity. KapSs_1.20
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage)
If [ignorance] were a real entity, the [Advaita] thesis would be undermined. KapSs_1.21
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage)
And there would follow a duality of a different kind. KapSs_1.22
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage)
If [ignorance] has the nature of both [real and unreal] — that is contradictory. KapSs_1.23
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage) — objection
No, because such a category is not cognized. KapSs_1.24
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage) — reply
We are not advocates of six categories like the <s>Vaiśeṣika</s> and others. KapSs_1.25
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage) — objection

children.text: aniyatatve 'pi nāyauktikasya saṃgrahaḥ, anyathā bālonmattādisamatvaṃ | KapSs_1.26 |
children.translated_text: Even without a fixed [number of categories], what is unreasonable is not to be accepted; otherwise there would be equality with children, madmen, and the like. KapSs_1.26
(Refutation of ignorance as the cause of bondage) — reply
Nor is this [bondage] caused by the coloring from beginningless sense-object [impressions]. KapSs_1.27
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage)

children.text: na bāhyābhyantarayoḥ uparajyopañjaka bhāvo 'pi deśavyavadhānāt srughnastha pāṭaliputrasthayoriva | KapSs_1.28 |
children.translated_text: There is no relation of coloring and being colored between the external and the internal, due to spatial separation — like [the case of] one residing in <s>Srughna</s> and one in <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>. KapSs_1.28
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage)
Since both obtain coloring in one place only, there is no [consistent] arrangement. KapSs_1.29
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage)
If [you say it is] due to unseen [merit/demerit]. KapSs_1.30
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage) — objection
No, because of the simultaneous conjunction of the two, the relation of benefactor and beneficiary [cannot be established]. KapSs_1.31
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage) — reply
If [you say it is] like the actions [performed for] a son. KapSs_1.32
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage) — objection

children.text: nāsti hi tatra sthira eka ātmā yo garbhādhānādikarmaṇā saṃskriyate | KapSs_1.33 |
children.translated_text: No, for there is no permanent, single self there that is refined by acts such as conception and the like. KapSs_1.33
(Refutation of sense-object impressions as the cause of bondage) — reply
Because no permanent effect is established, [all things are] momentary. KapSs_1.34
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else) — objection
No, because it contradicts recognition. KapSs_1.35
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else) — reply
And because it conflicts with scripture and reasoning. KapSs_1.36
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
And because the example is not established. KapSs_1.37
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
Between two things arising simultaneously, there is no cause-effect relation. KapSs_1.38
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
Upon the destruction of the prior, the subsequent would be impossible. KapSs_1.39
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
In the presence of that, [the effect] would be impossible; and because of deviation from both [alternatives], it is not [established]. KapSs_1.40
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
Mere prior existence does not establish a necessary [causal] rule. KapSs_1.41
(Refutation of the doctrine of momentariness regarding bondage and all else)
Reality is not consciousness-only, because of the perception of external [objects]. KapSs_1.42
(Refutation of the consciousness-only nature of bondage and all else)
In the absence of that [external object], there would be absence of that [consciousness]; then [everything would be] void. KapSs_1.43
(Refutation of the consciousness-only nature of bondage and all else)

children.text: śūnyaṃ tattvaṃ, bhāvo vinaśyati, vastudharmatvāt vināśasya | KapSs_1.44 |
children.translated_text: Reality is void; existence perishes, because destruction is a property of real things. KapSs_1.44
(Refutation of the doctrine of universal voidness) — objection
This is mere denial by the ignorant. KapSs_1.45
(Refutation of the doctrine of universal voidness) — reply
This [voidness doctrine] too [is refuted], because it is equally disadvantageous to both sides. KapSs_1.46
(Refutation of the doctrine of universal voidness)
Either way, it fails to serve any human purpose. KapSs_1.47
(Refutation of the doctrine of universal voidness)
Not through a particular mode of movement [of the self]. KapSs_1.48
(Refutation of a particular movement of the self as the cause of bondage)
Because for an actionless [self], that is impossible. KapSs_1.49
If [the self] were material, it would share the properties of a pot and the like — this contradicts the [Sāṃkhya] thesis. KapSs_1.50
(Refutation of a particular movement of the self as the cause of bondage)
(Refutation of a particular movement of the self as the cause of bondage)
The scriptural statement about movement [of the self] is due to conjunction with limiting adjuncts, like space. KapSs_1.51
(Refutation of a particular movement of the self as the cause of bondage)
Not through <s>karma</s> (action) either, because it is not a property of that [self]. KapSs_1.52
(Refutation of karma as the cause of bondage)
If [bondage] were a property of something other [than the self], there would be over-extension. KapSs_1.53
(Refutation of karma as the cause of bondage)
And there would be contradiction with scriptures declaring [the self to be] without qualities, etc. KapSs_1.54
(Refutation of karma as the cause of bondage)
Even the conjunction of that [Puruṣa with Prakṛti] is due to non-discrimination; [hence] there is no equality [with other theories]. KapSs_1.55
(Non-discrimination as the cause of the conjunction of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is alone the cause of bondage)
From its specific cause, the cessation of that [non-discrimination occurs], like darkness [being dispelled by light]. KapSs_1.56
(Discriminative knowledge alone is the cause of the destruction of non-discrimination)
Since non-discrimination from <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is primary, when it ceases, other non-discriminations also cease. KapSs_1.57
(Discriminative knowledge alone is the cause of the destruction of non-discrimination)
[Bondage] is not merely verbal — it is a real principle, because of the persistence of the mind. KapSs_1.58
(Even bondage residing in the mind, reflected onto <s>Puruṣa</s>, is removable through direct self-realization)
Nor is it contradicted by reasoning, like one confused about directions, or through indirect knowledge. KapSs_1.59
(Even bondage residing in the mind, reflected onto <s>Puruṣa</s>, is removable through direct self-realization)
For imperceptible things, knowledge is through inference, just as of fire through smoke and the like. KapSs_1.60
(The inferential nature of <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>)

children.text: satvarajastamasāṃ sāmyāvasthā prakṛtiḥ, prakṛtermahān, mahāto 'haṅkāraḥ, ahaṅkārāt pañcatanmātrāṇi, ubhayamindriyaṃ tanmātrebhyaḥ,sthūlabhūtāni puruṣaḥ iti pañcaviṃśatirgaṇaḥ | KapSs_1.61 |
children.translated_text: The state of equilibrium of <s>sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s> is <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); from <s>Prakṛti</s> arises <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle); from <s>Mahat</s>, <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle); from <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) and both sets of <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs); from the <s>tanmātras</s>, the gross elements; and <s>Puruṣa</s> — thus the group of twenty-five [principles]. KapSs_1.61
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
From the gross [elements, the existence] of the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements) [is inferred]. KapSs_1.62
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
From the external and internal [organs] and from those [tanmātras], [the existence] of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) [is established]. KapSs_1.63
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
From that [Ahaṅkāra, the existence] of the inner instrument [is established]. KapSs_1.64
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
From that, [the existence] of <s>Prakṛti</s> [is established]. KapSs_1.65
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
[The existence] of <s>Puruṣa</s> [is established] because composite [things] serve another's purpose. KapSs_1.66
(Establishment of the twenty-five principles)
At the root there is no [further] root; therefore the root [i.e., <s>Prakṛti</s>] is without a root. KapSs_1.67
(<s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the root of the entire universe)
Even through a succession [of causes], [everything] culminates in one [root]; therefore [the distinction of names] is merely nominal. KapSs_1.68
(<s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the root of the entire universe)
The assemblage of <s>Prakṛti</s> comprises both [the manifest and unmanifest]. KapSs_1.69
(<s>Prakṛti</s> alone is the root of the entire universe)
Because of the threefold qualification of seekers, there is no [universal] rule. KapSs_1.70
(The reason for discriminative contemplation not being universal)
The first evolute, called <s>Mahat</s> (the great principle) — that is the mind. KapSs_1.71
(The nature of the <s>Mahat</s> principle)
The last [evolute in the series] is <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle). KapSs_1.72
(The nature of the <s>Ahaṅkāra</s> principle)
The subsequent [principles] are effects of that [Ahaṅkāra]. KapSs_1.73
(Though the <s>tanmātras</s> and others are effects of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, their being effects of <s>Prakṛti</s> is also justified)
The primary causality [of Prakṛti operates] through that [intermediate cause], even in a succession — like an atom. KapSs_1.74
(Though the <s>tanmātras</s> and others are effects of <s>Ahaṅkāra</s>, their being effects of <s>Prakṛti</s> is also justified)
When both [cause and effect] pre-exist, upon the removal of one, conjunction with the other [occurs]. KapSs_1.75
(The determinant of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone being the cause of all)
What is limited cannot be the material cause of everything. KapSs_1.76
(The determinant of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone being the cause of all)
And because scripture declares the origination from that [Prakṛti]. KapSs_1.77
(The determinant of <s>Prakṛti</s> alone being the cause of all)
From a non-entity, no real entity can be established. KapSs_1.78
(Refutation of void as the cause of the universe, and of the voidness of the universe)
Because [the world] is not sublated and because it is produced from an untainted cause, it is not a non-entity. KapSs_1.79
(Refutation of void as the cause of the universe, and of the voidness of the universe)

children.text: bhāve tadyogena tatsiddhiḥ, abhāve tadabhāvāt kutastarāṃ tatsiddhiḥ | KapSs_1.80 |
children.translated_text: If [the cause] exists, through conjunction with it, that [effect] is established; if [the cause] does not exist, due to its absence, how much less can that [effect] be established? KapSs_1.80
(Refutation of void as the cause of the universe, and of the voidness of the universe)
Not from <s>karma</s> (action), because it cannot serve as the material cause. KapSs_1.81
(Refutation of karma as the material cause of the universe)

Nor is that [cessation of suffering] established through scriptural [ritual] means either; because of the possibility of recurrence due to [results] being yet to be accomplished, it fails to serve the [supreme] human purpose. KapSs_1.82
(Refutation of worldly and Vedic rituals as the cause of the supreme human purpose)
There is a scriptural declaration of non-return for one who has attained discrimination. KapSs_1.83
From suffering [comes more] suffering — like sprinkling water [on one already wet]; there is no release from inertia. KapSs_1.84
(Refutation of worldly and Vedic rituals as the cause of the supreme human purpose)
(Refutation of worldly and Vedic rituals as the cause of the supreme human purpose)
In both desire-prompted and non-desire-prompted [rites], there is no difference in [both] being [means] to be accomplished. KapSs_1.85
(Refutation of worldly and Vedic rituals as the cause of the supreme human purpose)

children.text: vijamuktasya bandhadhvaṃsamātraṃ, paraṃ na samānatvaṃ | KapSs_1.86 |
children.translated_text: For the liberated-while-living, [liberation] is merely the destruction of bondage; beyond that, there is no equivalence [with absolute liberation]. KapSs_1.86

The ascertainment of an object — whether of both [subject and object] or of either one — that is proximate and unerring, is valid knowledge (<s>pramā</s>); that which is the most effective instrument for it is the threefold means of valid knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>). KapSs_1.87
(The nature of valid knowledge and the number of means of valid knowledge)
(Refutation of worldly and Vedic rituals as the cause of the supreme human purpose)
Because everything is established through the establishment of these [three means], there is no need to establish additional [means]. KapSs_1.88
(The nature of valid knowledge and the number of means of valid knowledge)

children.text: yat saṃbaddhaṃ sat tadākārollekhi vijñānaṃ tat pratyakṣaṃ | KapSs_1.89 |
children.translated_text: That cognition which, being connected [with an object] that exists, reflects the form of that [object] — that is <s>pratyakṣa</s> (perception). KapSs_1.89
(Definition of perception)
There is no defect [in this definition], because the perception of <s>yogins</s> is non-external [i.e., supersensory]. KapSs_1.90
(Definition of perception)
There is no defect, because of the connection with extraordinary power obtained regarding subtle objects. KapSs_1.91
(Definition of perception)
Because <s>Īśvara</s> (God) is not established. KapSs_1.92
(Refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> in that context)
Because neither among the liberated nor the unliberated is there such [an Īśvara], that [existence] is not established. KapSs_1.93
(Refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> in that context)
In either case, [Īśvara] would be an ineffective agent. KapSs_1.94
(Refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> in that context)

children.text: muktātmanaḥ praśaṃsā upāsā siddhasya vā | KapSs_1.95 |
children.translated_text: The praise of a liberated soul, or the worship of a perfected being [is what scripture intends, not Īśvara]. KapSs_1.95
(Refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> in that context)
The superintendence [attributed to Īśvara] is due to the proximity of that [Puruṣa], like a magnet. KapSs_1.96
(Refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s> in that context)
Even in the specific effects, [this applies] to individual souls. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.97 |
(As a subsidiary of that: refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s>)
Since [the soul] is of the nature of one who is already accomplished, the teaching of the meaning of sentences [is sufficient for knowledge], from the [innate] capacity to know. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.98 |
(As a subsidiary of that: refutation of the existence of <s>Īśvara</s>)

children.text: antaḥ karaṇasya tadujjvalitatvāt lohavat adhiṣṭhātṛtvaṃ | KapSs_1.99 |
children.translated_text: Because the internal organ becomes illuminated by that [<s>Puruṣa</s>], like iron [by a magnet], it has the quality of being the presider. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.99 |
(The internal organ itself is the principal presider)
The knowledge of one who has the vision of a necessary connection is inference. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.100 |
(Definition of inference)
The instruction of a trustworthy person is verbal testimony (<s>śabda</s>). | <s>KapSs</s> 1.101 |
(Definition of verbal testimony)
The establishment of both [<s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>] is through the means of valid knowledge; the teaching of that [follows]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.102 |
(The fruit of ascertaining the nature of the means of valid knowledge)
The establishment of both [is also] from what is seen in general (<s>sāmānyatodṛṣṭa</s>). | <s>KapSs</s> 1.103 |
(Determination of the specific nature of inference based on general observation)
Experience terminates in consciousness. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.104 |
(The faultless nature of the means of valid knowledge)
Even for a non-agent, there is the experience of fruits, like [the enjoyment of] food and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.105 |
(Resolution of the doubt regarding the difference of locus between agency and the experience of fruits)
Or, from non-discrimination, the apprehension of fruit [belongs to] the agent, since that [agency] is established thereby. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.106 |
(Resolution of the doubt regarding the difference of locus between agency and the experience of fruits)
Neither [is the case] in the declaration of the truth. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.107 |
(Conditions for <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest being beyond the range of the senses)
An object [may be] a non-object [of perception] due to excessive distance and the rest, through the abandonment and reception of the sense organ. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.108 |
(Conditions for <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest being beyond the range of the senses)
Due to subtlety, that is not perceived. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.109 |
(Conditions for <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest being beyond the range of the senses)
Its apprehension [is established] from the observation of its effects. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.110 |
(Conditions for <s>Prakṛti</s> and the rest being beyond the range of the senses)
If [one objects that its] non-establishment [follows] from the disagreement among disputants— | <s>KapSs</s> 1.111 |
(Examination of <s>satkāryavāda</s>), objection:
Even so, from one point of view, [there is] the establishment of one or the other; there is no denial. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.112 |
(Examination of <s>satkāryavāda</s>), reply:
And because the fallacy of threefold contradiction would follow. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.113 |
(Examination of <s>satkāryavāda</s>)
There is no arising of the non-existent, like a horn of a man. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.114 |
(Refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s>)
Because of the restriction of the material cause. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.115 |
(Refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s>)
Because of the impossibility of everything [arising] from everything at all times. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.116 |
(Refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s>)
Because a capable [cause] produces what it is capable [of producing]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.117 |
(Refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s>)
And because of the [effect's] having the nature of the cause. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.118 |
(Refutation of <s>asatkāryavāda</s>)
If [one objects that] there is no connection of existence with [further] existence— | <s>KapSs</s> 1.119 |
(Justification of the effecthood of what exists), objection:
The [distinction between] usage and non-usage is not based on manifestation. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.120 |
(Justification of the effecthood of what exists), reply:
Destruction is dissolution into the cause. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.121 |
(The nature of destruction)
The search is successive, like the seed and sprout. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.122 |
(Avoidance of infinite regress in the manifestation view)
The fault is the same as for origination. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.123 |
Having a cause, non-eternal, non-pervasive, active, manifold, dependent—[such] is the mark [of an effect]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.124 |
(The nature of an effect)
(Avoidance of infinite regress in the manifestation view)
Its establishment [is] directly, or from non-difference, or from the commonality of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and the rest, or from the designation of the principal [cause]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.125 |
(The nature of an effect)
Being constituted of the three <s>guṇas</s>, being non-conscious, and the rest—[these are common] to both [cause and effect]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.126 |
(Similarities and dissimilarities between cause and effect)
Through pleasure, displeasure, despondency, and the rest—the mutual dissimilarity of the <s>guṇas</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.127 |
(Similarities and dissimilarities between cause and effect)

children.text: ladhvaidi dharmaiḥ sādharmyaṃ ca guṇānāṃ | KapSs_1.128 |
children.translated_text: And the similarity of the <s>guṇas</s> through the properties of lightness and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.128 |
(Similarities and dissimilarities between cause and effect)
From being other than both [<s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s>], the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest, like a pot and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.129 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
From [their] finitude. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.130 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
From [their] co-occurrence. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.131 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
And from [their] capacity. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.132 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
In the absence of that, [the cause must be either] <s>Prakṛti</s> or <s>Puruṣa</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.133 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
If they were other than those two, there would be vacuity. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.134 |
(Justification of the effecthood of <s>Mahat</s> and the rest)
The inference of the cause from the effect [is established] because of their co-existence. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.135 |
(The method of inferring the cause from the effects)
The unmanifest (<s>avyakta</s>) [is known] from the mark [of its effects, as] having three <s>guṇas</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.136 |
(Dissimilarity of <s>Prakṛti</s> from its effects)
Since that [<s>Prakṛti</s>] is established from its being the cause of those [effects], there is no denial. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.137 |
(Dissimilarity of <s>Prakṛti</s> from its effects)
In general, since there is no dispute, [the <s>guṇas</s>] are not proof, like a [commonly accepted] quality. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.138 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
<s>Puruṣa</s> is distinct from the body and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.139 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Because composite things serve another's purpose. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.140 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Because of the opposite of [having] three <s>guṇas</s> and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.141 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
And because of [the need for] a presider. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.142 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Because of [the need for] an experiencer (<s>bhoktṛ</s>). | <s>KapSs</s> 1.143 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
And because activity [of <s>Prakṛti</s>] is for the purpose of <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation). | <s>KapSs</s> 1.144 |
(Proof of the existence of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Since consciousness cannot belong to the insentient, [<s>Puruṣa</s> is] consciousness. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.145 |
(The nature of <s>Puruṣa</s> as consciousness)
Because of being without <s>guṇas</s>, consciousness is not a property [of the self]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.146 |
(Refutation of the property-property-bearer relation between consciousness and the self)
There is no denial of what is established by <s>śruti</s> (scripture), because of the direct knowledge of that. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.147 |
(Refutation of the property-property-bearer relation between consciousness and the self)
[<s>Puruṣa</s>] is the witness of deep sleep and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.148 |
(Refutation of the property-property-bearer relation between consciousness and the self)
From the arrangement of birth and the rest, the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.149 |
(Proof of the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>)
Even with difference of limiting adjuncts, the connection of one [self] with many [is possible], like space with pots and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.150 |
(Proof of the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>)
The limiting adjunct is differentiated, but not the one who possesses it. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.151 |
(Proof of the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>)

children.text: evamekatvena parivartamānasya na viruddha dharmādhyāsaḥ | KapSs_1.152 |
children.translated_text: Thus, for one who transforms as a unity, there is no superimposition of contradictory properties. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.152 |
(Proof of the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>)
Even if another's property [is there], the establishment of that through superimposition does not [follow], because of [its] unity. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.153 |
(Proof of the plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s>)
There is no contradiction with the <s>śrutis</s> of non-duality, because [those refer to] the universal. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.154 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
For one who knows the cause of bondage, through that vision, [the appearance is] not of that nature [i.e., not real]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.155 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
There is no non-perception by the sighted because of the vision of the blind. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.156 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
<s>Vāmadeva</s> and others were liberated—non-duality [is not negated]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.157 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
Since in the beginningless [past] there was always non-existence [of liberation], it will be so [in the future] also. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.158 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
As now, so everywhere—there is no absolute annihilation. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.159 |
(Justification of the doctrine of the oneness of the self)
[<s>Puruṣa</s>] is distinct from both forms [of <s>Prakṛti</s>—manifest and unmanifest]. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.160 |
Witness-hood [arises] from direct connection. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.161 |
(The eternally uniform nature of the selves)
(The eternally uniform nature of the selves)
[It is] eternally liberated. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.162 |
(The eternally uniform nature of the selves)
And [it has] indifference. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.163 |
(The eternally uniform nature of the selves)
Agency [is attributed to <s>Puruṣa</s>] due to coloring (<s>uparāga</s>), from the proximity of consciousness, from the proximity of consciousness. | <s>KapSs</s> 1.164 |

children.text: (vastutattvaviparītataya puruṣe kartṛtāyāḥ buddhau jñātṛtāyāśca bhāne hetuḥ), pradhānakārya
children.translated_text: (The cause of the appearance of agency in <s>Puruṣa</s> and the appearance of knowership in <s>buddhi</s>, which is contrary to the real truth of things). Effects of <s>Pradhāna</s>:
The [activity] of <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of the liberation of the liberated, or for its own purpose. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.1 |
(The factors that serve as the cause of <s>Prakṛti</s>'s creation of the world)
Since that is established even for the detached [<s>Puruṣa</s>]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.2 |
(The factors that serve as the cause of <s>Prakṛti</s>'s creation of the world)
That [liberation] is not accomplished by mere hearing, because of the strength of beginningless <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.3 |
(The factors that serve as the cause of <s>Prakṛti</s>'s creation of the world)
Or, [creation is] for each [<s>Puruṣa</s>] individually, like [a king] with many servants. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.4 |
(The factors that serve as the cause of <s>Prakṛti</s>'s creation of the world)
When the reality of <s>Prakṛti</s> [is understood], the superimposition on <s>Puruṣa</s> is established [as false]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.5 |
(Refutation of creatorship in <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Since that [non-creatorship of <s>Puruṣa</s>] is established from the effects. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.6 |
(Refutation of creatorship in <s>Puruṣa</s>)
The purposeful direction toward the conscious [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is the governing principle, like the removal of a thorn. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.7 |
(Refutation of creatorship in <s>Puruṣa</s>)
Even in the conjunction of another, its establishment [arises] not directly, like in the smelting of iron. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.8 |
(Refutation of creatorship in <s>Puruṣa</s>)
The conjunction of attachment and detachment—and creation [results from that]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.9 |
In the order beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, [creation] of the five gross elements. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.10 |
(The creation beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation)
(The primary efficient cause for creation)
Since creation is for [<s>Puruṣa</s>'s] own purpose, the activity of these [evolutes] is not for their own purpose. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.11 |
(The creation beginning with <s>Mahat</s>, for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>'s liberation)
Space and time [arise] from <s>ākāśa</s> (ether) and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.12 |
(The creation of space and time)
Determination is <s>buddhi</s> (intellect). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.13 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>Mahat</s> principle)
Its effects are <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.14 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>Mahat</s> principle)
From the coloring of <s>Mahat</s>, [there arises] its opposite [i.e., <s>adharma</s> etc.]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.15 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>Mahat</s> principle)
Self-conceit is <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.16 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> principle)
Its effects are the eleven [sense organs] and the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.17 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> principle)
The <s>sāttvika</s> group of eleven proceeds from the modified (<s>vaikṛta</s>) <s>ahaṅkāra</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.18 |
(The nature, effects, etc., of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> principle)
The group of eleven is internal, [consisting of] the organs of action and the organs of knowledge. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.19 |
(The nature of the sense organs)
From the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) that they are products of <s>ahaṅkāra</s>, they are not elemental. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.20 |
(The nature of the sense organs)
The <s>śruti</s> about deity-abodes is not [about] the originator. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.21 |
(The nature of the sense organs)
From the <s>śruti</s> of their origination and from the observation of their destruction. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.22 |
(The impermanence of the sense organs)
The sense organ is beyond the senses; [the error] of the confused is regarding the seat [i.e., the physical organ]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.23 |
(Refutation of the view that the physical globes are the sense organs)
Even when there is difference of power, since difference is established, there is no unity. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.24 |
(Refutation of the doctrine of a single sense organ)
There is no contradiction of supposition with what is established by valid means of knowledge. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.25 |
(Refutation of the doctrine of a single sense organ)
And <s>manas</s> (mind) is of a twofold nature. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.26 |
(The twofold nature of <s>manas</s> as both cognitive and active)
The diversity [of <s>manas</s>] is due to the differentiation of the transformations of the <s>guṇas</s>, like [different] states. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.27 |
(The twofold nature of <s>manas</s> as both cognitive and active)
Form and the rest, up to impurity—[these are the objects] of both [types of senses]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.28 |
(The objects of the sense organs)
Seeing and the rest [belong to] the self; instrumentality [belongs to] the sense organs. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.29 |
(The sense organs serve the self as instruments)
The three [internal organs] have their own distinctive [functions]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.30 |
(The specific and common functions of the three internal organs)
The common function of the organs [is] the five vital breaths beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.31 |
(The specific and common functions of the three internal organs)
The function of the sense organs is both sequential and simultaneous. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.32 |
(There is no fixed rule of sequentiality for the function of the senses)
The mental modifications are fivefold, either afflicted or non-afflicted. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.33 |
Upon the cessation of those [modifications], [<s>Puruṣa</s>] is at peace, with coloring removed, abiding in its own nature. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.34 |
(In the state of withdrawal of modifications, <s>Puruṣa</s> abides in its own nature)
(The five types of mental modifications)
Like a gem [placed] near a flower [takes on its color]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.35 |
(In the state of withdrawal of modifications, <s>Puruṣa</s> abides in its own nature)
Though the production of instruments is for <s>Puruṣa</s>'s purpose, [their activity is also] from the manifestation of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.36 |
(The condition for the activity of the sense organs)
Like a cow for its calf. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.37 |
(The condition for the activity of the sense organs)
The instruments are thirteenfold, due to sub-divisions. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.38 |
(The thirteenfold nature of the instruments)
Among the sense organs, due to possessing the quality of being the most efficient agent, like an axe. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.39 |
(The thirteenfold nature of the instruments)

children.text: dvayoḥ pradhānaṃ mano lokavat bhṛtyavargeṣu | KapSs_2.40 |
children.translated_text: Between the two [groups], <s>manas</s> (mind) is the chief, like [a minister] among groups of servants in the world. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.40 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
Because of [its] invariable [involvement]. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.41 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
Likewise, because of being the substratum of all impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>). | <s>KapSs</s> 2.42 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
And from memory and inference. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.43 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
Since it is possible, [the priority] is not inherent. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.44 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
The secondary and primary status is relative, [varying] according to the specific activity. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.45 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
Since that [body] has been earned by <s>karma</s>, the endeavor is for its [<s>Puruṣa</s>'s] purpose, as in the world. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.46 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
When there is equal engagement in action, the primacy of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) [is established], as in the world. | <s>KapSs</s> 2.47 |
(The determination of the secondary and primary status among the instruments)
Detachment and the rest—
From the non-specific, the undertaking of the specific [arises]. | <s>KapSs</s> 3.1 |
(From the five <s>tanmātras</s>, the gross creation that is the seed of <s>saṃsāra</s>)
From that, [the creation] of the body. | <s>KapSs</s> 3.2 |
(The gross creation, which is the seed of <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration), arises from the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements))
From that seed arises <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration). | KapSs_3.3 |
(The gross creation, which is the seed of <s>saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration), arises from the five <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements))
And until <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) arises, the <s>aviśeṣas</s> (non-specific elements) continue to operate. | KapSs_3.4 |
Experience belongs to one [<s>Puruṣa</s>], the other [<s>Prakṛti</s>] serves a different purpose. | KapSs_3.5 |
(<s>Saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration) terminates in <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
(<s>Saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration) terminates in <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
At present, [the <s>Puruṣa</s>] is liberated from both. | KapSs_3.6 |
(<s>Saṃsṛti</s> (transmigration) terminates in <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))

children.text: mātāpitṛjaṃ sthūlaṃ prāyaśaḥ itaranna tathā | KapSs_3.7 |
children.translated_text: The gross [body] is born from mother and father, generally; the other [subtle body] is not so. | KapSs_3.7 |
(The distinction between the gross body and the subtle body)
Because it arises prior [to the gross body], it is an effect of that; experience belongs to one [body], not to the other. | KapSs_3.8 |
(The distinctions between the gross body and the subtle body)
The <s>liṅga</s> (subtle body) consists of seventeen [elements]. | KapSs_3.9 |
(The <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body) and its effects)
The difference in manifestation is due to the particularity of <s>karma</s> (action). | KapSs_3.10 |
(The <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body) and its effects)
The gross body, which is the abode and support of that [subtle body], is spoken of as that or not-that. | KapSs_3.11 |
(The gross body depends on the subtle body as its superintendent and support)
It [the gross body] has no independence without that [subtle body], like a shadow or like a painting. | KapSs_3.12 |
(The necessity of the existence of the subtle body as superintendent of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s>)
Even though corporeal, there is no obstruction due to its conjunction [with the subtle body], like a boat. | KapSs_3.13 |
(The necessity of the existence of the subtle body as superintendent of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s>)
Its measure is atomic, because of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) describing its nature thus. | KapSs_3.14 |
(The measure of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body))
And because of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) declaring it to be made of food. | KapSs_3.15 |
(The measure of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body))
The transmigration of the <s>liṅgas</s> (subtle bodies) is for the sake of <s>Puruṣa</s>, like a cook for a king. | KapSs_3.16 |
(The transmigration of the <s>liṅgaśarīra</s> (subtle body) serves the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>)
The body is composed of five <s>bhūtas</s> (elements). | KapSs_3.17 |
(Different views regarding the nature of the gross body)
Some say it is composed of four <s>bhūtas</s> (elements). | KapSs_3.18 |
(The non-existence of consciousness as a property of the elements)
Others say it is composed of one <s>bhūta</s> (element). | KapSs_3.19 |
(The non-existence of consciousness as a property of the elements)
Consciousness is not inherent [in the elements], because it is not observed in each one separately. | KapSs_3.20 |
(The non-existence of consciousness as a property of the elements)
And because of the absence of manifestation, death, and so forth [in consciousness]. | KapSs_3.21 |
(The non-existence of consciousness as a property of the elements)

If [it is argued that consciousness arises] like the intoxicating power [of ingredients individually non-intoxicating], [we reply that] since it is observed in each individually, its arising in combination [is not analogous]. | KapSs_3.22 |
(The non-existence of consciousness as a property of the elements)
From <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) comes <s>mukti</s> (liberation). | KapSs_3.23 |
(<s>Mukti</s> (liberation) and <s>bandha</s> (bondage) arise from <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>viparyaya</s> (error) respectively)
<s>Bandha</s> (bondage) arises from <s>viparyaya</s> (error). | KapSs_3.24 |
(<s>Mukti</s> (liberation) and <s>bandha</s> (bondage) arise from <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) and <s>viparyaya</s> (error) respectively)
Because the cause is fixed, neither combination nor alternative [of means] is applicable. | KapSs_3.25 |
(<s>Tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) alone is the cause of liberation)
Just as in dream and waking, through the illusory and the non-illusory, liberation of <s>Puruṣa</s> does not come from both. | KapSs_3.26 |
(<s>Tattvajñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) alone is the cause of liberation)
Even of the other [meditative knowledge], there is no permanence. | KapSs_3.27 |
(The absence of liberating power in knowledge that is merely <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation))
Even in what is willed [through meditation], it is the same. | KapSs_3.28 |
(The absence of liberating power in knowledge that is merely <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation))
Through the accumulation of contemplation, for the purified one, everything [becomes possible] like <s>Prakṛti</s>. | KapSs_3.29 |
(The fruit of <s>upāsanā</s> (meditation))
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the removal of attachment. | KapSs_3.30 |
(<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) as a means to the knowledge that is the means of liberation)
Its accomplishment is through the cessation of mental modifications (<s>vṛttinirodha</s>). | KapSs_3.31 |
(The means of accomplishing <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation))
Its accomplishment is through <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), <s>āsana</s> (posture), and the performance of one's own duties. | KapSs_3.32 |
(The means of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and their characteristics)
<s>Nirodha</s> (restraint) is achieved through expulsion and retention [of breath]. | KapSs_3.33 |
(The means of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and their characteristics)
<s>Āsana</s> (posture) is that which is steady and comfortable. | KapSs_3.34 |
(The means of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and their characteristics)
One's own duty is the performance of the actions prescribed for one's own <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life). | KapSs_3.35 |
(The means of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and their characteristics)
Through <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) and <s>abhyāsa</s> (practice). | KapSs_3.36 |
(For the principal aspirant, there is no need for the five [practices] beginning with <s>yama</s>)
The divisions of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) are five. | KapSs_3.37 |
(The classification of <s>viparyaya</s> (error) as the cause of bondage)
<s>Aśakti</s> (incapacity) is of twenty-eight kinds. | KapSs_3.38 |
(The divisions of <s>aśaktis</s> (incapacities), which are the causes of <s>viparyaya</s> (error))
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is of nine kinds. | KapSs_3.39 |
(The classification of <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), which produce intellectual incapacity and capability respectively)
<s>Siddhi</s> (attainment) is of eight kinds. | KapSs_3.40 |
(The classification of <s>tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) and <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), which produce intellectual incapacity and capability respectively)
The sub-divisions are as stated before. | KapSs_3.41 |
Similarly for the other [<s>aśakti</s>]. | KapSs_3.42 |
(Some elaboration on <s>viparyaya</s>, <s>aśakti</s>, <s>tuṣṭi</s>, and <s>siddhi</s>)
(Some elaboration on <s>viparyaya</s>, <s>aśakti</s>, <s>tuṣṭi</s>, and <s>siddhi</s>)
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> (contentment) is of nine kinds, due to the distinction of <s>ādhyātmika</s> (pertaining to the self) and others. | KapSs_3.43 |
(Some elaboration on <s>viparyaya</s>, <s>aśakti</s>, <s>tuṣṭi</s>, and <s>siddhi</s>)
<s>Siddhi</s> (attainment) is of eight kinds, through <s>ūha</s> (reasoning) and other [means]. | KapSs_3.44 |
(Some elaboration on <s>viparyaya</s>, <s>aśakti</s>, <s>tuṣṭi</s>, and <s>siddhi</s>)
Not the one without the elimination of the other. | KapSs_3.45 |
(Attainments through austerity and so forth are not true <s>siddhi</s> (attainment of reality))
The varieties are divine and so forth. | KapSs_3.46 |
(The varieties of creation beginning with the divine, and their limits)
From <s>Brahmā</s> down to a blade of grass, creation is produced by that [<s>Prakṛti</s>], until <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) arises. | KapSs_3.47 |
(The varieties of creation beginning with the divine, and their limits)
Above, <s>sattva</s> predominates. | KapSs_3.48 |
(Varieties of creation according to the predominance of <s>guṇas</s>)
<s>Tamas</s> predominates at the bottom. | KapSs_3.49 |
(Varieties of creation according to the predominance of <s>guṇas</s>)
In the middle, <s>rajas</s> predominates. | KapSs_3.50 |
(Varieties of creation according to the predominance of <s>guṇas</s>)
The activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is due to the variety of <s>karma</s> (actions), like a pregnant woman or a slave. | KapSs_3.51 |
(The cause of the variety of creation)
Repetition [of creation] occurs even there, due to progressively higher conjunction, and is to be abandoned. | KapSs_3.52 |
(All creations up to liberation are to be abandoned)
The suffering of old age, death, and so forth is the same [in all states of existence]. | KapSs_3.53 |
(All creations up to liberation are to be abandoned)
There is no fulfillment through dissolution into the cause, because [one] rises again, like a submerged person. | KapSs_3.54 |
(Even <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>) is not absolute liberation)
Even when there is no [manifest] effect, connection with it [remains] due to subjection [to <s>Prakṛti</s>]. | KapSs_3.55 |
(Even <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>) is not absolute liberation)
For he [the <s>prakṛtilīna</s>] is omniscient and omnipotent. | KapSs_3.56 |
(Even <s>prakṛtilaya</s> (dissolution into <s>Prakṛti</s>) is not absolute liberation)
The establishment of such an <s>Īśvara</s> (lord) is thus established. | KapSs_3.57 |
(The one dissolved in <s>Prakṛti</s> alone has the status of a created <s>Īśvara</s> (lord))
The creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is for the sake of another [<s>Puruṣa</s>], because it itself is not an experiencer. | KapSs_3.58 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))
Like a camel carrying saffron. | KapSs_3.59 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))
Even though non-conscious, the activity of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) is like that of milk. | KapSs_3.60 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))
Or like <s>karma</s> (action), due to the observation of [activity in] time and such [non-conscious entities]. | KapSs_3.61 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))
Its activity is from its own nature, without deliberate intention, like a servant. | KapSs_3.62 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))
Or because it is impelled by <s>karma</s> (action), beginninglessly. | KapSs_3.63 |
(The rationale and purpose of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter))

children.text: viviktabodhāt sṛṣṭinivṛttiḥ pradhānasya sūdavat pāke | KapSs_3.64 |
children.translated_text: Through the knowledge of discrimination, the cessation of creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) [occurs], like a cook after the cooking [is done]. | KapSs_3.64 |
(The cause of the cessation of creation)
Because of the fault of mutual dependence between the two. | KapSs_3.65 |
(The cause of the cessation of creation)
<s>Apavarga</s> (liberation) is the indifference of one or both of the two [<s>Puruṣa</s> and <s>Prakṛti</s>]. | KapSs_3.66 |
(The cause of the cessation of creation)

children.text: anyasṛṣṭyuparāge 'pi na virajya (ma) te prabuddharajjutatvasyevoragaḥ | KapSs_3.67 |
children.translated_text: Even when one creation ceases, [<s>Prakṛti</s>] does not desist [from others], like a serpent for one who has awakened to the rope-nature. | KapSs_3.67 |
(The cessation of one particular creation does not obstruct the continuation of another)
And because of the connection with <s>karma</s> (action) as the cause. | KapSs_3.68 |
(The cessation of one particular creation does not obstruct the continuation of another)
Even when there is no need [on the part of <s>Puruṣa</s>], ignorance is the cause of <s>Prakṛti's</s> assistance. | KapSs_3.69 |
(Explanation of the regulator of <s>Prakṛti's</s> activity and cessation)
Even though engaged [in activity], cessation [of <s>Prakṛti</s>] occurs when the purpose is fulfilled, like a dancer. | KapSs_3.70 |
(Explanation of the regulator of <s>Prakṛti's</s> activity and cessation)
Even when the fault is known, <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) does not approach [again], like a chaste woman. | KapSs_3.71 |
(Explanation of the regulator of <s>Prakṛti's</s> activity and cessation)
Bondage and liberation do not absolutely belong to <s>Puruṣa</s>, except through ignorance. | KapSs_3.72 |
(Bondage and liberation do not truly belong to the self)
Because of the straightforward nature of <s>Prakṛti</s>, and because of association [with it], like an animal. | KapSs_3.73 |
(Bondage and liberation do not truly belong to the self)

children.text: rūpaiḥ saptabhiḥ ātmānaṃ badhnāti pradhānaṃ kośakāravadvimocayetyekarūpeṇa | KapSs_3.74 |
children.translated_text: <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter) binds itself by seven forms, and liberates by one form, like a silkworm. | KapSs_3.74 |
(The causes of bondage and liberation)
The causality of ignorance [as producing bondage] does not [mean] the negation of what is observed. | KapSs_3.75 |
(The causes of bondage and liberation)
Through the practice of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles), by the negation 'not this, not this,' through renunciation, the accomplishment of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) [is achieved]. | KapSs_3.76 |
(The practice of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) alone is the cause of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
There is no fixed rule, due to the differences among aspirants. | KapSs_3.77 |
(The practice of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) alone is the cause of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
Due to the continued operation of sublated [ignorance], even from intermediate <s>viveka</s> (discrimination), experience [of suffering continues]. | KapSs_3.78 |
And [there is] <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living). | KapSs_3.79 |
(Only a particular [complete] <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) is the means of final deliverance)
(Only a particular [complete] <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) is the means of final deliverance)
Its accomplishment is established by the fact that there are teachers and taught. | KapSs_3.80 |
(The means of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living))
And [this is confirmed by] <s>śruti</s> (scripture). | KapSs_3.81 |
(The means of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living))
Otherwise, there would be a blind succession [of the ignorant leading the ignorant]. | KapSs_3.82 |
(The means of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living))
[The liberated one] maintains the body like the [continued] rotation of a wheel. | KapSs_3.83 |
(The means of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living))
That accomplishment [of continued embodiment] is due to a trace of <s>saṃskāras</s> (impressions). | KapSs_3.84 |
(The means of <s>jīvanmukti</s> (liberation while living))
Through <s>viveka</s> (discrimination), upon the cessation of all suffering, one becomes fulfilled -- not by any other [means], nor from any other [cause]. | KapSs_3.85 |
(For <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>viveka</s> (discrimination) alone is the cause of fulfillment)
<s>Ākhyāyikā</s> (Illustrative Stories)
Like a prince, through the teaching of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles). | KapSs_4.1 |
(The teaching of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) is the cause of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
Like [the story of] the <s>piśāca</s> (demon), even when the teaching concerns another subject. | KapSs_4.2 |
(The teaching of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) is the cause of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
Repetition [is necessary], because the teaching is given many times. | KapSs_4.3 |
(The teaching of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) is the cause of <s>viveka</s> (discrimination))
Like father and son, because both are observed [to be subject to death]. | KapSs_4.4 |
(In some cases, from inference, the understanding of the perishability of the body and the removal of ignorance arise)
Like a hawk, one experiences happiness and suffering through renunciation and separation respectively. | KapSs_4.5 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
Like a snake shedding its skin. | KapSs_4.6 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
Or like one whose hand has been cut off. | KapSs_4.7 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
Contemplation of what is not a [true] means leads to bondage, like [the story of King] <s>Bharata</s>. | KapSs_4.8 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)

children.text: bahubhiryoge virodhaḥ rāgādibhiḥ kumārī kaṅkaṇa (śaṅkha) vat | KapSs_4.9 |
children.translated_text: In the conjunction of many [desires], there is obstruction to <s>yoga</s> (concentration), due to attachment and other [passions], like the maiden's bangles. | KapSs_4.9 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
Even with two, it is the same. | KapSs_4.10 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
One who is free from expectation is happy, like <s>Piṅgalā</s>. | KapSs_4.11 |
Even without effort, one is happy in another's house, like a serpent. | KapSs_4.12 |
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
(Mental qualities as accessories to the accomplishment of knowledge)
Even in studying many scriptures and serving many teachers, one should extract the essence, like a bee. | KapSs_4.13 |
(The necessity of extracting the essence)
For one whose mind is not one-pointed, there is no loss of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), like an arrow-maker. | KapSs_4.14 |
(The necessity of one-pointedness)
From transgressing established rules, there is futility, as in the world. | KapSs_4.15 |
(The necessity of not transgressing the rules prescribed by scripture)
Even when there is forgetfulness of those [rules], it is like a frog [swallowed by a snake]. | KapSs_4.16 |
(The necessity of remembering the rules prescribed by scripture)
Even by hearing the teaching, there is no fulfillment without reflection, like <s>Virocana</s>. | KapSs_4.17 |
(The necessity of reflecting on what has been heard)
This is seen in the case of [both] <s>Indra</s>. | KapSs_4.18 |
(The necessity of reflecting on what has been heard)

children.text: praṇatibrahmacaryopasarpaṇāni kṛtvā siddhiḥ bahukālāt tadvat | KapSs_4.19 |
children.translated_text: Having performed prostration, <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibate studentship), and service [to the teacher], attainment comes after a long time, like that [story of <s>Indra</s>]. | KapSs_4.19 |
(Service to the teacher)
There is no fixed rule regarding time, like <s>Vāmadeva</s>. | KapSs_4.20 |
(There is no restriction of time, place, and so forth for the attainment of knowledge)
Through the worship of superimposed forms, [attainment comes] indirectly by tradition, like those who worship through sacrifices. | KapSs_4.21 |
(There is no restriction of time, place, and so forth for the attainment of knowledge)
Even upon attaining the other [world], there is return, because of the <s>śruti</s> (scripture) regarding birth through the five-fire doctrine. | KapSs_4.22 |
(Meditations that cause return)
For the dispassionate one, the abandonment of what is to be rejected and the adoption of what is to be accepted [is natural], like a swan separating milk [from water]. | KapSs_4.23 |
(The qualification for the attainment of knowledge)
Or through the attainment of extraordinary <s>yoga</s>, like that [swan]. | KapSs_4.24 |
(The qualification for the attainment of knowledge)
There should be no license [to act as one pleases] when attachment is present, like a parrot [trapped in a cage]. | KapSs_4.25 |
(The defects of attachment and the means of subduing them)
Bound by the conjunction of <s>guṇas</s>, like a parrot [on a perch]. | KapSs_4.26 |
(The defects of attachment and the means of subduing them)
Attachment is not pacified through enjoyment, like a sage [whose desire increased]. | KapSs_4.27 |
(The defects of attachment and the means of subduing them)
Through seeing the defects in both [enjoyment and attachment]. | KapSs_4.28 |
(The faults of attachment and the means for their pacification)
Instruction [is fruitless] in one whose mind is impure, like the sprouting of a seed in barren [soil]. | KapSs_4.29 |
(The faults of attachment and the means for their pacification)
Not even a mere reflection [appears in it], like a dirty mirror. | KapSs_4.30 |
(The faults of attachment and the means for their pacification)
Even in one born of that [lineage], there is no aptitude for that—like a lotus [born] from mud. | KapSs_4.31 |
(The faults of attachment and the means for their pacification)

children.text: na bhūtiyoge 'pi kṛtakṛtyatā upāsyasiddhivat upāsyasiddhivat | KapSs_4.32 |
children.translated_text: Even in the attainment of supernatural powers (<s>bhūti</s>), there is no state of having accomplished one's purpose—like [the incompleteness of] the attainment of the deity being worshipped. | KapSs_4.32 |
(The eight supernatural powers also do not equal liberation)
Victory over the opponent's doctrine.
The performance of auspicious rites (<s>maṅgalācaraṇa</s>) [is established] from the conduct of the learned, from the observation of results, and from scripture (<s>śruti</s>). | KapSs_5.1 |
(The purpose of performing auspicious rites)
The production of results does not [depend] on being superintended by <s>Īśvara</s> (God), because [results] are established by <s>karma</s> (action). | KapSs_5.2 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Superintendence [is exercised] for one's own benefit, as in the world. | KapSs_5.3 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Otherwise [it would be] like a worldly lord. | KapSs_5.4 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Or [the term 'Īśvara' is merely] conventional (<s>pāribhāṣika</s>). | KapSs_5.5 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Without desire (<s>rāga</s>), that [creation] is not established, because of [each effect] having a specifically determined cause. | KapSs_5.6 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Even if that [desire] is present, [God] is not eternally liberated. | KapSs_5.7 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
If [one says it is] through connection with the power of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), then [God] would incur bondage (<s>saṅga</s>). | KapSs_5.8 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
If [creation follows] from mere existence [of God], then there would be omnipotence [at all times]. | KapSs_5.9 |
(The non-existence of God as bestower of results)
Because of the absence of a valid means of knowledge (<s>pramāṇa</s>), that [God's existence] is not established. | KapSs_5.10 |
(The absence of proof for God)
Because of the absence of a relation [between God and the world], there is no inference (<s>anumāna</s>) [for God]. | KapSs_5.11 |
(The absence of proof for God)
Scripture (<s>śruti</s>) also [supports] <s>Pradhāna</s> as the cause. | KapSs_5.12 |
(The absence of proof for God)
For one who is unattached, there is no connection with the power of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance). | KapSs_5.13 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
If that [ignorance] is present [in Brahman], and that [ignorance] is established [as causing bondage], there would be mutual dependence (<s>anyonyāśraya</s>). | KapSs_5.14 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
It is not like the seed and sprout, because scripture declares <s>saṃsāra</s> to have a beginning. | KapSs_5.15 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
If [<s>avidyā</s>] is other than <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), there would be the consequence of the sublation of <s>Brahman</s>. | KapSs_5.16 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
If there is no sublation, [knowledge would be] fruitless. | KapSs_5.17 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
If [<s>avidyā</s>] is sublated by <s>vidyā</s>, then the world (<s>jagat</s>) too [would be sublated] in the same way. | KapSs_5.18 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
If [<s>avidyā</s>] has the nature of that [Brahman], it would have a beginning. | KapSs_5.19 |
(Refutation of the view that bondage is caused by ignorance)
There is no denial of real entities (<s>dharmas</s>), because of the variety of the effects of <s>Prakṛti</s>. | KapSs_5.20 |
(Refutation of the view that the activity of Pradhāna is caused by karma)
That [Pradhāna as cause] is established by scripture, inferential marks (<s>liṅga</s>), and other [means]. | KapSs_5.21 |
(Refutation of the view that the activity of Pradhāna is caused by karma)
There is no restriction [to only one cause], because there is scope for other means of knowledge. | KapSs_5.22 |
(Refutation of the view that the activity of Pradhāna is caused by karma)
The same [applies] to both [sides of the argument]. | KapSs_5.23 |
(Refutation of the view that the activity of Pradhāna is caused by karma)
If establishment is from the purpose [served], then it is equal for both. | KapSs_5.24 |
(Refutation of the view that the activity of Pradhāna is caused by karma)
<s>Dharma</s> (merit) and the like are properties of the internal organ (<s>antaḥkaraṇa</s>). | KapSs_5.25 |
(Dharma and adharma are properties of the internal organ)
And there is no absolute negation of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) and the like. | KapSs_5.26 |
(The impropriety of absolutely negating sattva and other guṇas and their properties)
The cognition of pleasure [arises] from the conjunction of five members. | KapSs_5.27 |
(The impropriety of absolutely negating sattva and other guṇas and their properties)
The establishment of a relation does not [come] from a single apprehension. | KapSs_5.28 |
(The nature of pervasion and its proof), [Objection:]
Pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) is the invariable co-occurrence of two properties, or of one [with the other]. | KapSs_5.29 |
(The nature of pervasion and its proof), [Conclusion:]
It is not a separate category, because of the involvement of the construction of [mere] entities. | KapSs_5.30 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
It arises from inherent power (<s>nijaśakti</s>)—so [say] the <s>Ācāryas</s> (teachers). | KapSs_5.31 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
It is a connection with a superimposed power (<s>ādheyaśakti</s>)—so [says] <s>Pañcaśikha</s>. | KapSs_5.32 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
There is no restriction to inherent power (<s>svarūpaśakti</s>), because of the consequence of redundancy. | KapSs_5.33 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
Because of the consequence of purposelessness with respect to the particular. | KapSs_5.34 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
And because of inapplicability in cases of shoots and the like. | KapSs_5.35 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
If superimposed power is established, [then] the connection with inherent power [also follows] by the same reasoning. | KapSs_5.36 |
(Refutation of others' views on the nature of pervasion)
The relation between word and meaning is the relation of signifier and signified (<s>vācya-vācaka-bhāva</s>). | KapSs_5.37 |
(Proving the validity of verbal testimony)
The relation is established by three [means]. | KapSs_5.38 |
(The means of grasping linguistic capacity in ordinary usage and the Vedas)

children.text: na kārye niyamaḥ ubhayathā darśanāt | KapSs_5.39 |
children.translated_text: There is no restriction to [a single type of] effect, because both types are observed. | KapSs_5.39 |
(The means of grasping linguistic capacity in ordinary usage and the Vedas)
One who has become proficient in worldly [language] comprehends the meaning of the <s>Veda</s>. | KapSs_5.40 |
(The means of grasping linguistic capacity in ordinary usage and the Vedas)
Not by [those] three [means is the Veda established], because of the non-human origin (<s>apauruṣeyatva</s>) of the <s>Veda</s>; and because its meaning too is beyond the senses. | KapSs_5.41 |
(Refutation of the view that the Veda has a supersensible subject matter), [Objection:]

children.text: na yajñādeḥ svarūpato dharmatvaṃ vaiśiṣṭyāt | KapSs_5.42 |
children.translated_text: Sacrifice (<s>yajña</s>) and the like are not <s>dharma</s> by their own nature, because of [their] distinctive character. | KapSs_5.42 |
(Refutation of the view that the Veda has a supersensible subject matter), [Conclusion:]
The inherent power [of words] is ascertained through proficiency (<s>vyutpatti</s>). | KapSs_5.43 |
(The determination of grasping the power of Vedic words)
That [validity] is established because [words] generate cognition with respect to fitting and unfitting [objects]. | KapSs_5.44 |
(The determination of grasping the power of Vedic words)
The <s>Vedas</s> are not eternal, because scripture declares [them to be] products. | KapSs_5.45 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
Nor are [they] of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>), because of the non-existence of a person who could be their author. | KapSs_5.46 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
Because both the liberated and the unliberated are unfit [to be authors]. | KapSs_5.47 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
Eternality does not [follow] from non-human origin, like a sprout and the like. | KapSs_5.48 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
Even for those [eternal entities], if that [human origin] were admitted, there would be the consequence of contradiction with observation and the like. | KapSs_5.49 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
That regarding which, even without [direct] observation, the cognition of its being a product arises—that is of human origin (<s>pauruṣeya</s>). | KapSs_5.50 |
(Refutation of the eternality and non-human origin of the Vedas)
The validity [of the Vedas] is intrinsic (<s>svataḥ prāmāṇya</s>), because of [their] manifestation through inherent power. | KapSs_5.51 |
(The intrinsic validity of the Vedas)
There is no appearance of the non-existent—like a hare's horn. | KapSs_5.52 |
Nor [can they] be [considered] existent, because sublation is observed. | KapSs_5.53 |
(The guṇas are neither absolutely non-existent nor indeterminable)
(The guṇas are neither absolutely non-existent nor indeterminable)
Nor [are they] indeterminable (<s>anirvacanīya</s>), because of the absence of that [category]. | KapSs_5.54 |
(The guṇas are neither absolutely non-existent nor indeterminable)
There is no erroneous cognition (<s>anyathākhyāti</s>), because of self-contradiction. | KapSs_5.55 |
(Refutation of the theory of erroneous cognition)
[The theory of] cognition of both the existent and non-existent (<s>sadasatkhyāti</s>) [is refuted] because of [simultaneous] sublation and non-sublation. | KapSs_5.56 |
(Refutation of the sadasatkhyāti theory)
Sound (<s>śabda</s>) is not of the nature of <s>sphoṭa</s> (the meaning-bearing linguistic unit), because of [its] being cognized and not cognized [successively]. | KapSs_5.57 |
(Refutation of the sphoṭa theory)
There is no eternality of sound, because [its] being a product is cognized. | KapSs_5.58 |
(Refutation of the eternality of phonemes)
[Objection:] The manifestation of a previously established existent [phoneme]—like a pot by a lamp. | KapSs_5.59 |
(Refutation of the eternality of phonemes), [Objection:]
If [this is based on] the <s>satkārya</s> doctrine (pre-existence of the effect in the cause), that would be proving what is [already] established. | KapSs_5.60 |
(Refutation of the eternality of phonemes), [Conclusion:]
There is no non-duality of the Self (<s>ātman</s>), because of the inferential marks [of plurality] and the cognition of their differences. | KapSs_5.61 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
Nor [is there] multiplicity of selves, because of contradiction with direct perception. | KapSs_5.62 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
Nor [is it] both, for the same reason. | KapSs_5.63 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
The [apparent] otherness or non-distinction [of selves] in that [body] is [due to] non-discrimination. | KapSs_5.64 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
Neither the Self (<s>ātman</s>), nor <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), nor both [together] is the material cause of the world—because [the Self] is unattached. | KapSs_5.65 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
The one [Self] cannot have the nature of both bliss and consciousness, because of the difference between the two. | KapSs_5.66 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
The [bliss in liberation is] secondary (<s>gauṇa</s>), [being merely] the cessation of suffering. | KapSs_5.67 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)
The praise of liberation is [intended] for the dull-witted. | KapSs_5.68 |
(Refutation of non-duality of the Self)

children.text: na vyāpakatvaṃ manasaḥ karaṇatvādindriyatvādvā vāsyādivaccakṣurādivacca | KapSs_5.69 |
children.translated_text: The mind (<s>manas</s>) is not all-pervading—because of its being an instrument, like a chisel and the like; or because of its being a sense-organ, like the eye and the like. | KapSs_5.69 |
(Refutation of the partlessness, all-pervasiveness, and eternality of mind)
Because it is active and because scripture speaks of [its] movement. | KapSs_5.70 |
(Refutation of the partlessness, all-pervasiveness, and eternality of mind)
It is not without parts, because of its connection with those [parts]—like a pot. | KapSs_5.71 |
(Refutation of the partlessness, all-pervasiveness, and eternality of mind)
Everything other than <s>Prakṛti</s> and <s>Puruṣa</s> is impermanent. | KapSs_5.72 |
(The impermanence of everything other than Prakṛti and Puruṣa)
There is no acquisition of parts by what is partless, because scripture declares [it to be] without parts. | KapSs_5.73 |
(The impermanence of everything other than Prakṛti and Puruṣa)
Liberation is not the manifestation of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), because [the liberated Self] is without properties. | KapSs_5.74 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of manifestation of bliss)
Nor is it the destruction of special qualities—for the same reason. | KapSs_5.75 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of the destruction of special qualities)
There is no going to a special place for one who is without action. | KapSs_5.76 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of going to another world)
It is not the destruction of the coloring of form (<s>ākāra-uparāga</s>), because of the fault of momentariness (<s>kṣaṇikatva</s>) and the like. | KapSs_5.77 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of destruction of coloring, nor of total annihilation)
There is no total annihilation (<s>sarvocchitti</s>), because of the fault of being purposeless for the Self and the like. | KapSs_5.78 |
(The inappropriateness of liberation being of the nature of void and so on)
The same [applies to] emptiness (<s>śūnya</s>) as well. | KapSs_5.79 |
(The inappropriateness of liberation being of the nature of void and so on)

children.text: saṃyogāśca vibhāgāntā iti na deśādilābho 'pi | KapSs_5.80 |
children.translated_text: And since all conjunctions end in separation, there is no acquisition of a place (<s>deśa</s>) and the like either. | KapSs_5.80 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of a special lordship and the like)
There is no conjunction of a part with [what is] partless. | KapSs_5.81 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of dissolution)

Nor is there even the conjunction with <s>aṇimā</s> (power of becoming minute) and other [supernatural powers], because of their inevitable destruction—like the conjunction with other [impermanent things]. | KapSs_5.82 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of a special station of supernatural powers)
Nor is there conjunction with the station of <s>Indra</s> and others either—for the same reason. | KapSs_5.83 |
(Liberation is not of the nature of a special station of supernatural powers)
The sense-organs are not made of the gross elements (<s>bhūta</s>), because scripture declares [them to be] produced from <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (the ego-principle). | KapSs_5.84 |
(Refutation of the view that sense-organs are made of gross elements)
There is no restriction to six categories, nor is liberation [obtained] from knowledge of them. | KapSs_5.85 |
(Refutation of the fixed number of categories proposed by others, and that knowledge of them causes liberation)
The same [applies] to sixteen [categories] and so on as well. | KapSs_5.86 |
(Refutation of the fixed number of categories proposed by others, and that knowledge of them causes liberation)
Atoms (<s>aṇu</s>) are not eternal, because scripture declares [them to be] effects. | KapSs_5.87 |
(Refutation of the eternality of atoms)
They are not without parts, because of [their] being products. | KapSs_5.88 |
(Refutation of the eternality of atoms)
There is no restriction of perception to [dependence upon] form (<s>rūpa</s>). | KapSs_5.89 |
Magnitude is not fourfold; by two [magnitudes] alone, that [variation] is explained. | KapSs_5.90 |
(Proof of universals and their nature)
(Determination of the nature of magnitude and other [qualities])
Even though [things are] impermanent, recognition (<s>pratyabhijñāna</s>) of universals (<s>sāmānya</s>) [occurs] because of their connection with stability. | KapSs_5.91 |
(Proof of universals and their nature)
Therefore there is no denial of that [universal]. | KapSs_5.92 |
(Proof of universals and their nature)
It is not of the nature of exclusion of the other (<s>anyānivṛtti</s>), because of the cognition of a positive entity. | KapSs_5.93 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
Similarity (<s>sādṛśya</s>) is not a separate category, because it is perceived through direct perception. | KapSs_5.94 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
Or [it is] the manifestation of inherent power, because it is perceived as distinctive. | KapSs_5.95 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
There is also no relation between name and named (<s>saṃjñā</s> and <s>saṃjñin</s>). | KapSs_5.96 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
The relation [between them] is not [self-established], because both [relata] are impermanent. | KapSs_5.97 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
The relation is not unproduced (<s>aja</s>), because it is contradicted by the valid means of knowledge that grasps the property-bearer. | KapSs_5.98 |
(Refutation of similarity being a separate category)
There is no <s>samavāya</s> (inherence), because of the absence of proof. | KapSs_5.99 |
(Refutation of inherence)
In both cases [inherence is not established], because otherwise-explained—neither by perception nor by inference. | KapSs_5.100 |
(Refutation of inherence)
Action (<s>kriyā</s>) is not necessarily inferential only, because there is direct perception of what is nearest—of that which possesses those [actions]. | KapSs_5.101 |
(Refutation of the claim that action is necessarily only inferential)
The body is not made of the five gross elements (<s>pāñcabhautika</s>), because many [elements] cannot serve as the material cause [of one thing]. | KapSs_5.102 |
(Refutation of the body being made of five elements)

children.text: na sthūlamiti niyamaḥ ātivāhikasyāpi vidyāmānatvāt | KapSs_5.103 |
children.translated_text: There is no restriction that [the body must be] gross, because the transmigrating [body] (<s>ātivāhika</s>) also exists. | KapSs_5.103 |
(Refutation of grossness as a general property of bodies)
The <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs) do not illumine unattained objects, because either there is no contact or there is contact with everything. | KapSs_5.104 |
(Determination of the contact-based operation of the sense organs)

children.text: na tejo 'pasarpaṇāt taijasa cakṣuḥ vṛttitastatsiddheḥ | KapSs_5.105 |
children.translated_text: The eye is not of the nature of <s>tejas</s> (fire/light) because of the movement of light; the eye being a modification of <s>tejas</s>, its functioning is established through <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification). | KapSs_5.105 |
(Determination of the contact-based operation of the sense organs)
The functioning of <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification) is established by the sign that it illumines objects that have been reached. | KapSs_5.106 |
