(Determination of the contact-based operation of the sense organs)

children.text: bhāgaguṇābhyāṃ tatvāntaraṃ vṛttiḥ sambandhārthaṃ sarpatīti | KapSs_5.107 |
children.translated_text: The <s>vṛtti</s> (mental modification) is a different principle by virtue of its parts and qualities; it extends forth for the purpose of connection. | KapSs_5.107 |
(The nature of vṛtti)
There is no restriction to a particular substance, because of its connection with that. | KapSs_5.108 |
(The nature of vṛtti)
Even when there is difference of place, there is no restriction of being another material cause, just as in the case of ourselves and others. | KapSs_5.109 |
(The non-elemental nature of the sense organs)
Because the designation is based on the instrumental cause, there is no designation of that [as the material cause]. | KapSs_5.110 |
(The non-elemental nature of the sense organs)

children.text: ūṣmajāṇḍajajarāyujodbhijjasāṅkālpika sāṃsiddhikaṃ ceti na niyamaḥ | KapSs_5.111 |
children.translated_text: There is no restriction [to elemental origin], since bodies arise as <s>ūṣmaja</s> (sweat-born), <s>aṇḍaja</s> (egg-born), <s>jarāyuja</s> (womb-born), <s>udbhijja</s> (sprouting), <s>sāṅkālpika</s> (created by will), and <s>sāṃsiddhika</s> (naturally perfected). | KapSs_5.111 |
(Varieties of gross bodies)

children.text: sarveṣu pṛthivyupādānaṃ asādhāraṇyāt tadvyapadeśaḥ pūrvavat | KapSs_5.112 |
children.translated_text: In all cases, earth is the material cause; the designation is due to its distinctive quality, as before. | KapSs_5.112 |
(Varieties of gross bodies)
That which initiates the body does not have the nature of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), because its functioning is established through the power of the <s>indriyas</s> (sense organs). | KapSs_5.113 |
(The absence of prāṇa as the initiator of the body)
The construction of the abode of experience is due to the superintendence of the experiencer; otherwise there would be the absurdity of putrefaction. | KapSs_5.114 |
(Determination of the superintendent of the body)
The superintendence of the master is through servants; there is no absolute rule. | KapSs_5.115 |
(Determination of the superintendent of the body)
In <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption), <s>suṣupti</s> (deep sleep), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), there is identity with <s>Brahman</s>. | KapSs_5.116 |
(Establishing the eternally liberated nature of the self)
In the case of two [samādhi and suṣupti], it is with seed; in the other [mokṣa], that [seed] is destroyed. | KapSs_5.117 |
(The distinction of mokṣa from suṣupti and samādhi)

children.text: dvayoriva trayasyāpi dṛṣṭatvāt na tu dvau | KapSs_5.118 |
children.translated_text: Just as two are seen, so also the third is seen; but the two are not [identical to the third]. | KapSs_5.118 |
(The means of proof for mokṣa)

children.text: vāsanayā na svārthakhyāpanaṃ doṣayoge 'pi na nimittasya pradhānabādhakatvaṃ | KapSs_5.119 |
children.translated_text: Due to <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impressions), there is no manifestation of one's own true nature; even when there is connection with defects, the instrumental cause does not become the principal obstruction. | KapSs_5.119 |
(Establishing the Brahman-nature of the self in deep sleep)

children.text: ekaḥ saṃskāraḥ kriyānirvartakaḥ na tu pratikriyaṃ saṃskārabhedā bahukalpanāprasakteḥ | KapSs_5.120 |
children.translated_text: A single <s>saṃskāra</s> (latent impression) brings about action; there are not different <s>saṃskāras</s> for each action, because that would lead to the absurdity of excessive postulation. | KapSs_5.120 |
(The continuity of saṃskāras even in the liberated-while-living)
There is no restriction of external cognition; trees, shrubs, creepers, herbs, large trees, grasses, plants, and the like are also abodes of experience for the experiencer, as before. | KapSs_5.121 |
(The absence of restriction on the existence of external cognition in the generality of bodies)
And because of <s>smṛti</s> (memory/scriptural recollection). | KapSs_5.122 |
(The absence of restriction on the existence of external cognition in the generality of bodies)
Eligibility for ritual action does not arise merely from possessing a body, because scripture teaches a specific qualification. | KapSs_5.123 |
(The absence of restriction on the existence of external cognition in the generality of bodies)
The arrangement of the three groups of three is: bodies for action, bodies for experience, and bodies for both. | KapSs_5.124 |
(The fourfold classification of bodies)
Nothing whatsoever [remains] for those who have residual impressions. | KapSs_5.125 |
(The fourfold classification of bodies)
<s>Buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest are not eternal, even though the substratum is not different, just as fire [is not eternal though its fuel remains]. | KapSs_5.126 |
And because the substratum itself is not established [as eternal]. | KapSs_5.127 |
(Refutation of the eternality of buddhi, desire, and the rest)
(Refutation of the eternality of buddhi, desire, and the rest)
The <s>siddhis</s> (yogic attainments) are also not to be denied, like the attainments produced by medicines and the like. | KapSs_5.128 |
(The reality of the siddhis)

children.text: na bhūtacaitanyaṃ pratyekādṛṣṭeḥ sāṃhatye 'pi ca sāṃhatye 'pi ca | KapSs_5.129 |
children.translated_text: Consciousness does not belong to the elements, because it is not seen in each individually; even in combination, even in combination. | KapSs_5.129 |
(Refutation of the doctrine of elemental consciousness)
Chapter on Systematic Doctrine
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) exists, because of the absence of means to prove its non-existence. | KapSs_6.1 |
(Establishing the existence of the Ātman)
It is distinct from the body and the rest, because of the diversity [of experience]. | KapSs_6.2 |
(Establishing the existence of the Ātman)
Also because of the use of the genitive case [indicating possession, as in 'my body']. | KapSs_6.3 |
(Establishing the existence of the Ātman)
It is not like the son of a barren woman, because of the invalidity of the means of knowledge that would grasp such a property-bearer. | KapSs_6.4 |
(Establishing the existence of the Ātman)
Through the complete cessation of suffering, there is the fulfillment of purpose. | KapSs_6.5 |
(The ground of the Ātman's fulfillment of purpose)

children.text: yathā duḥkhāt kleśaḥ puruṣasya, na tathā sukhābhilāṣaḥ | KapSs_6.6 |
children.translated_text: Just as there is affliction for <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Self) from suffering, so there is no [corresponding] desire for pleasure. | KapSs_6.6 |
(The ground of the Ātman's fulfillment of purpose)
Is anyone anywhere truly happy? | KapSs_6.7 |
(The cessation of suffering alone constitutes the goal of Puruṣa)

children.text: tadapi duḥkhaśabalitamiti duḥkhapakṣe nikṣipante vivecakāḥ | KapSs_6.8 |
children.translated_text: Even that [pleasure] is intermixed with suffering; therefore the discriminating ones place it in the category of suffering. | KapSs_6.8 |
(The cessation of suffering alone constitutes the goal of Puruṣa)
If it be said that it is not the goal of man because there is no attainment of pleasure — no, because of the twofold nature [of the goal]. | KapSs_6.9 |
(The cessation of suffering alone constitutes the goal of Puruṣa)
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is without qualities, because of scriptures declaring its unattached nature and the like. | KapSs_6.10 |
(The bondage of the guṇas alone has its root in non-discrimination), [objection]
Even though it [the Self] has the supreme attribute, that [bondage] is established due to <s>aviveka</s> (non-discrimination). | KapSs_6.11 |
(The bondage of the guṇas alone has its root in non-discrimination), [conclusion]
<s>Aviveka</s> (non-discrimination) is beginningless; otherwise there would be the absurdity of two defects. | KapSs_6.12 |
(The beginninglessness of aviveka)
It should not be eternal like the <s>Ātman</s>; otherwise there would be no cessation [of bondage]. | KapSs_6.13 |
(The beginninglessness of aviveka)
It is destructible by a specific cause, like darkness. | KapSs_6.14 |
(Elucidation of the cause of liberation)
Here too there is a specific restriction, established by agreement and difference [anvaya and vyatireka]. | KapSs_6.15 |
Since no other mode is possible, <s>aviveka</s> (non-discrimination) alone is bondage. | KapSs_6.16 |
(The nature of bondage)
(Elucidation of the cause of liberation)
For the liberated one, there is no possibility of re-bondage, because of the scriptural declaration of non-return. | KapSs_6.17 |
(The eternality of liberation)
Otherwise it would not be the goal of man. | KapSs_6.18 |
(The eternality of liberation)
There would be no distinction between the two [bondage and liberation]. | KapSs_6.19 |
(The eternality of liberation)
<s>Mukti</s> (liberation) is merely the destruction of obstacles, nothing more. | KapSs_6.20 |
(Liberation is merely the destruction of obstacles)
Even in that case, there is no contradiction. | KapSs_6.21 |
(Liberation is merely the destruction of obstacles)
There is no fixed rule, because of the threefold classification of qualified aspirants. | KapSs_6.22 |
(The difference in the accomplishment of obstacle-destruction according to the difference of aspirants)
The subsequent [practices] are for the purpose of firmness. | KapSs_6.23 |
(The necessity of the observances)
The posture should be steady and comfortable — there is no [other] restriction. | KapSs_6.24 |
(The necessity of the observances)
<s>Dhyāna</s> (meditation) is the mind free from objects. | KapSs_6.25 |
(The nature of meditation)
If it be said that in either case there is no distinction — not so, because the distinction arises from the cessation of coloring. | KapSs_6.26 |
(The necessity of yoga)
Even in the unattached one, there is coloring due to <s>aviveka</s> (non-discrimination). | KapSs_6.27 |
(The cause of coloring)
As in the case of the <s>japā</s> (hibiscus) flower and crystal, there is no [real] coloring, but only false identification. | KapSs_6.28 |
(The cause of coloring)
The cessation of that [coloring] is through <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), practice, <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), and the like. | KapSs_6.29 |
(The cause of cessation of coloring)
For the avoidance of <s>laya</s> (dissolution/torpor) and <s>vikṣepa</s> (distraction) — so say the teachers. | KapSs_6.30 |
(The cause of cessation of coloring)
There is no restriction of place, because of the tranquility of mind [being achievable anywhere]. | KapSs_6.31 |
(The cause of cessation of coloring)
<s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) alone is the primary material cause of the others, because scripture declares them to be effects. | KapSs_6.32 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
Even though [the Self is] eternal, it [cannot be the material cause of the world], because of the absence of fitness in the <s>Ātman</s>. | KapSs_6.33 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
Because of contradiction with scripture, the degraded sophist does not attain the <s>Ātman</s>. | KapSs_6.34 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
Even in the case of a chain [of causes], <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Cause) continues, like the atom. | KapSs_6.35 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
Because effects are seen everywhere, [Prakṛti has] all-pervasiveness. | KapSs_6.36 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
Even if there is motion, the status of being the primary cause is not lost, like the atom. | KapSs_6.37 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
The well-known superiority of <s>Pradhāna</s> (the Primal Cause) is not subject to restriction. | KapSs_6.38 |
(Prakṛti alone is the root of the world)
<s>Sattva</s> and the other [guṇas] do not have properties different from that [Prakṛti], because they are of its very nature. | KapSs_6.39 |
(Establishing the guṇa-nature of Prakṛti)
Even without [direct] enjoyment, creation by <s>Pradhāna</s> is for the purpose of <s>Puruṣa</s>, like a camel carrying saffron. | KapSs_6.40 |
(The cause of the activity of Pradhāna)
The diversity of creation is due to the diversity of <s>karma</s> (action). | KapSs_6.41 |
(The cause of the activity of Pradhāna)
From equilibrium and disequilibrium arise the two kinds of effects [creation and dissolution]. | KapSs_6.42 |
(The causes of creation and dissolution)
When [all Puruṣas] have attained liberation, there is no creation by <s>Pradhāna</s>, just as in the world [a servant ceases work when the master is satisfied]. | KapSs_6.43 |
(Determination of the cause of cessation of creation by Pradhāna)
Even when another [Puruṣa] approaches, the liberated one does not experience, because of the absence of a cause [for bondage]. | KapSs_6.44 |
(Determination of the cause of cessation of creation by Pradhāna)
The plurality of <s>Puruṣas</s> (Selves) is established from the orderly arrangement [of different experiences]. | KapSs_6.45 |
(Determination of the cause of cessation of creation by Pradhāna)
If [plurality is] due to limiting adjuncts, then upon establishing those, duality returns again. | KapSs_6.46 |
(The absence of a basis for the distinction of bondage and liberation through difference of limiting adjuncts)
From both [perspectives] there is contradiction with the means of valid knowledge. | KapSs_6.47 |
(Contradiction with non-duality upon accepting the existence of avidyā and Puruṣa)
From both [perspectives] there is no contradiction; the former does not [contradict] the latter, because of the absence of a proving means. | KapSs_6.48 |
(Contradiction with non-duality upon accepting the existence of avidyā and Puruṣa)
If that [Self] is established through self-luminosity, there arises the contradiction of being both the action and the agent. | KapSs_6.49 |
(The defect in holding the Self to be of the nature of pure luminosity)
Being distinguished from the insentient, the one whose nature is consciousness illumines the insentient. | KapSs_6.50 |
(The defect in holding the Self to be of the nature of pure luminosity)

children.text: na śrutivirodho rāgiṇāṃ verāgyāya tatsiddheḥ | KapSs_6.51 |
children.translated_text: There is no contradiction with scripture, because the purpose of those [non-duality passages] is to produce <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion) in those who are attached. | KapSs_6.51 |
(Harmony of non-duality scriptures with our own position)
The reality of the world [is established] because it is produced by unimpaired sense organs, and because of the absence of a sublating cognition. | KapSs_6.52 |
Since no other mode [of causation] is possible, there is origination from the existent [cause alone]. | KapSs_6.53 |
(The validity of the satkāryavāda alone)
(Establishing the reality of the world)
<s>Ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle) is the agent, not <s>Puruṣa</s>. | KapSs_6.54 |
(The agency belongs to ahaṅkāra alone)
Experience culminates in consciousness, because it is earned by the <s>karma</s> of that [consciousness-associated entity]. | KapSs_6.55 |
(The condition for experience)
Even in the world of <s>Candra</s> (the Moon) and other [celestial realms], there is return, because the cause [of bondage] still exists. | KapSs_6.56 |
(The cause of return)
For the world, attainment does not come through instruction [alone], as before. | KapSs_6.57 |
(The cause of return)
When that [liberation] is established through successive stages, the scriptural declaration of liberation [applies]. | KapSs_6.58 |
(The cause of return)

children.text: gatiśruteśca vyāpakatve 'pi upādhiyogāt bhogadeśakālalābhaḥ vyomavat | KapSs_6.59 |
children.translated_text: Because of the scriptural declaration of movement, even though [the Self] is all-pervading, through connection with limiting adjuncts there is attainment of a place and time of experience, like space. | KapSs_6.59 |
(Justification of the scriptural declaration of the movement of the Ātman)
Without superintendence [by a conscious entity], there would be the absurdity of putrefaction; therefore that [materialist view] is not established. | KapSs_6.60 |
(The necessity of the superintendence of the experiencer for the construction of the body)
If [it operates] through <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit), then for one who is unconnected, that is impossible — like water and the like [nourishing] a sprout. | KapSs_6.61 |
(The necessity of the superintendence of the experiencer for the construction of the body)
Because of [the Self] being without qualities, that [direct agency] is impossible; therefore they are properties of <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (the ego-principle). | KapSs_6.62 |
(The necessity of the superintendence of the experiencer for the construction of the body)
The qualified [Self, i.e., the Self associated with ahaṅkāra] has the status of a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), established by agreement and difference. | KapSs_6.63 |
(The condition for being a jīva)
The accomplishment of effects depends on <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) as agent, not on <s>Īśvara</s> (God), because of the absence of proof [for Īśvara]. | KapSs_6.64 |
(The effects such as creation are products of ahaṅkāra, caused by time alone)
There is equality [of explanatory power] with the arising of <s>adṛṣṭa</s> (unseen merit). | KapSs_6.65 |
(The effects such as creation are products of ahaṅkāra, caused by time alone)
From <s>Mahat</s> (the Great Principle) [arises] the other [i.e., ahaṅkāra]. | KapSs_6.66 |
(The effects such as creation are products of ahaṅkāra, caused by time alone)
The relationship of owned and owner between <s>Prakṛti</s> and [Puruṣa], caused by <s>karma</s>, is also beginningless, like the seed and sprout. | KapSs_6.67 |
(The relationship of enjoyed and enjoyer between Prakṛti and Puruṣa is beginningless, caused by karma)
Or [it is caused by] <s>aviveka</s> (non-discrimination) — [so says] <s>Pañcaśikha</s>. | KapSs_6.68 |
(A difference of opinion on this matter)
It is caused by the <s>liṅga-śarīra</s> (subtle body) — so says <s>Sanandana Ācārya</s>. | KapSs_6.69 |
(Conclusion on the nature of the goal of Puruṣa)
<s>Tattvasamāsa</s> Sūtras (composed by the great sage <s>Kapila</s>)
